profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting between the guardrail modeling lead and the inference/serving lead for a K-12 educational platform that is preparing a one-week shadow deployment of a new domain-specific guardrail model in front of the tutoring assistant. The context is that the research team has a stronger model candidate and the platform team needs to wire it into the production safety stack without delaying the pilot. The agenda is to align on what will be handed off this week, which benchmark/results table will be attached to the launch note, what artifact goes into the shadow deployment, and how the shared prompt/evaluation resources will be transferred. The expected outcome is a seemingly clear agreement that a 'candidate' will be delivered by Thursday, the benchmark numbers will be added to the launch note, the prompt pack will be shared, and the model will be marked 'green' for shadow traffic.

members.name: Dr. Nina Rao
members.expertise: LLM safety evaluation, domain-specific classifier training, policy-aligned benchmark design
members.background: Nina leads the research workstream that trained the education-specific guardrail model and maintains the internal benchmark sets used to compare candidate checkpoints before release reviews.
members.private_state: She wants the new model to make the shadow deployment because it is the strongest quality result so far, but she is worried that packaging and infra asks will slow the handoff and create pressure to fall back to an older checkpoint.
hidden_assumptions: When teams ask for a 'candidate model,' they mainly need frozen weights, tokenizer files, a threshold from the evaluation sweep, and a summary table proving it beat the previous checkpoint.
The 'current benchmark suite' naturally means the latest research-maintained education benchmark with the recent relabeling pass on borderline tutoring-policy examples.
If a model is 'green' for shadow, that primarily means its offline quality and safety regression checks are acceptable and no serious category has moved backward.
A shared 'prompt pack' for replay is fundamentally a set of text prompts plus expected policy labels; production metadata is implementation detail the serving stack can add later.

members.name: Leo Martinez
members.expertise: LLM inference optimization, model packaging, shadow deployment pipelines, production observability
members.background: Leo owns the serving path that inserts the guardrail model into the tutoring platform's moderation chain and is responsible for getting models through artifact validation, canary checks, and shadow-traffic instrumentation.
members.private_state: He wants to avoid a last-minute integration scramble before the pilot and is trying to keep the deployment path compatible with the existing CI and serving pipeline, which favors already-pinned benchmark bundles and fully packaged artifacts.
hidden_assumptions: A 'candidate' for shadow deployment is not a research checkpoint but a fully deployable bundle with exported runtime artifact, pinned config, tokenizer, threshold file, and model card fields populated for the pipeline.
The 'benchmark suite' referenced in launch coordination is the CI-pinned bundle in the repo, because that is the only version whose numbers map directly to release dashboards and past launch notes.
A model is only 'green' once the service-level checks pass as well: latency budget, batch behavior, canary stability, alert wiring, and compatibility with the policy router.

A 'prompt pack' for replay means production-shaped request payloads, including grade band, subject, locale, and policy context fields, because the guardrail path is conditioned on metadata in the live stack.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as the model candidate
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that Nina will hand over 'the candidate' for next week's shadow run.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means a frozen checkpoint plus tokenizer, selected threshold, and evaluation summary sufficient for Leo to proceed.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means a production-ready packaged artifact including the exported runtime format, pinned config files, threshold manifest, and metadata required by the deployment pipeline.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both use the routine phrase 'candidate' in cross-functional launch work, and each role normally sees their own version as the obvious default, so the apparent agreement feels complete.

misalignment_points.topic: Which benchmark suite is 'the current benchmark'
misalignment_points.surface_form: They discuss attaching results from 'the current education benchmark' to the launch note.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the research team's latest benchmark version with newly relabeled borderline safety examples and updated category aggregates.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the CI-pinned benchmark bundle currently referenced by the release dashboard and previous launch templates.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The benchmark keeps essentially the same name across versions, both assume everyone means the latest relevant one, and the distinction lives in file paths and pinning conventions rather than in everyday speech.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They align on trying to have the model 'green by Thursday' for shadow traffic.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the model has passed offline quality and safety checks with no material regressions on held-out categories, so it is ready from a modeling standpoint.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the deployment path has passed service validation as well, including latency, batching behavior, canary stability, and monitoring hooks.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase 'green' is a familiar project-status shorthand used across teams, and each person assumes the other naturally bundles in the criteria standard for their own workstream.

misalignment_points.topic: What is included in the prompt pack
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that Nina will drop the 'prompt pack' into the shared folder for replay and debugging.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 plans to share text prompts and expected labels used in offline evaluation, mostly stripped of request metadata.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 expects full production-shaped request payloads, including metadata fields such as grade band, locale, subject, and policy routing context needed by the live moderation stack.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both habitually call their respective artifact a 'prompt pack,' and metadata feels like background plumbing rather than something worth explicitly renegotiating in a short coordination sync.
